The Appendix A event, with an Appendix C kind (run.state.started) and the inbox state.
An imported commitment carries heimdall provenance (native id, native revision, import receipt).
FLAG is a verdict result (§10; pinned Saga contract REC-4); an escalated review leaves the combined verdict null.
A REJECT escalates even while the other position is unavailable, so an escalated combination with a null position verdict is valid.
Without a REJECT or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, combination stays null while a position's verdict is null.
A shadow prompt is logged, never sent, and ends expired with an expired response record.
guidance_rev is set on a guidance effect.
The kinds catalogue validates against its schema.
The namespaces catalogue validates against its schema.
Unknown keys reject the document (strict JSON); a project has no owner field.
Digests are lowercase sha256 hex.
Commitment state is open, blocked, satisfied, closed or abandoned.
Provenance source is heimdall, the only import source (ODIN-ADR-007).
ownership_generation starts at 1.
Checkpoints are a required field since ODIN-ADR-007; a missing key is reported at its own pointer.
Two failures are reported as a sorted list of pointers: a non-ULID owner and an evidence ref without evid:.
Backend is saga, local or desktop.
Limits are numbers >= 0.
Nested objects are strict too.
Auth mode is subscription, api or local (AGENTS.md §6; D24).
Every record has id, rev, created_at, updated_at (Appendix A).
A binding's subject is an assignment or a planning session.
An unreachable host makes a binding host_offline, never failed (ODIN-ADR-009).
Capabilities come from the adapter capability-matrix vocabulary.
Herdr access is local or ssh_machine.
Timestamps are UTC with a literal Z.
Request kinds are clarification, plan_approval, delegation_change, principle_change, desktop_action.
response is a reference ("response ref"), not an inline answer object.
The principal is a verified operator identity; Odin cannot approve.
A numeric UTC offset is not the canonical Z form.
Exactly two reviewer positions (ODIN-ADR-013).
The two positions are a and b.
Escalated leaves the combined verdict null (Appendix A).
Approved requires both positions to approve.
Combination stays null while a position's verdict is null; approved also needs both verdicts.
One review and at most one corrective re-review (D8; §10).
Probabilities are within 0..1.
Status is ok, unavailable, invalid, uncertain or timeout (§5; AC-09).
A class decision is about an event, an assignment or a planning session.
An override without a reason is refused (§4; AC-39).
snooze carries its until time (Appendix A).
In shadow mode a prompt is logged, never sent (§4).
A responded prompt carries its response record.
A typed rule is recorded with its version (<rule>@<version>).
held records dispatch_blocked_by (§9).
U is not a Crockford base32 character.
guidance_rev is set only for guidance effects; null otherwise (Appendix A).
Destinations are <target>:<operation>.
chat is odin/<project>, mimir or work/<name>.
Message kinds are the ten of §3.
A message's identity is (chat, i); it has no id field.
Scope keys are project, run, assignment, session, host, commitment.
This is envelope version 1.
A namespace outside the catalogue is a schema failure.
Source sequences are >= 0.
The inbox processing state is required.
$ in a pattern means end of string: a trailing newline does not pass (Python re's $ would allow it).
Duplicate keys reject the document at decoding; the error is the duplicated key's pointer.
An event carries a payload or an evidence ref; the anyOf failure is reported at the document root ("").
Both payload and payload_ref may be present.
run.state (the Appendix A example's spelling) matches the kind pattern but is not an Appendix C kind.
Schema validation runs first; the catalogue check runs only on a schema-valid envelope.
A kind is dotted lowercase segments.
A valid event in the odin_history namespace.
A valid event in the transcript_archive namespace.
A valid event in the surface_events namespace.
A valid event in the execution_ledger namespace.
Only the namespace's single writer may append to odin_history; nothing is appended.
Only the namespace's single writer may append to transcript_archive; nothing is appended.
Only the namespace's single writer may append to surface_events; nothing is appended.
Only the namespace's single writer may append to execution_ledger; nothing is appended.
A component that is no namespace's writer is refused.
The mirror is filled only from Saga's cursor, so a mirrored event carries its Saga sequence.
The writer check precedes the source_seq check.
The Saga adapter applies a cursor-delivered event to the mirror.
The service writer appends to odin_history.
The capture_module writer appends to transcript_archive.
The workstation_sensors writer appends to surface_events.
Even the namespace's own writer cannot amend an appended event; redaction is a tombstone message operation (§8).
Appended events are never deleted.
The adapter applies, never authors or amends a mirrored record.
A redelivered Telegram message is a counted no-op; the dedupe-key check runs before the sequence check.
A producer without a sequence is deduplicated by key alone; its cursor stays null.
A different dedupe key at a sequence the cursor has passed is still a duplicate.
A sequence at or below the cursor is a counted no-op; gaps above the cursor are accepted.
Cursors are per producer: equal sequences from different producers are independent.
Cursors and seen dedupe keys are per (namespace, producer): the inbox copy and the mirror copy are both accepted.
duplicates_counted is cumulative over the case; an event without a sequence leaves its producer's cursor unchanged.
Control messages first in received order, then the rest in received order; processed events are skipped.
return, take and pause are all direct commands; keeping them in one ordered batch preserves take-after-return.
Without control messages the order is the received order, not id order.
Nothing is replayed when every event is processed.
Processing is idempotent by event id; an unknown id is reported; replay skips what was processed.
Equal revisions pass.
A write based on an older revision is the 409 stale_revision; nothing changes.
Any mismatch is stale, including an expected revision from the future.
A write that depends on prior state must carry expected_revision.
A null expected_revision counts as missing.
The session acts under the commitment's current ownership generation.
A superseded session's writes fail with 409 stale_owner.
A retired session's writes fail even at the current generation.
Only retired is stale by state; a retiring session at the current generation may still write.
Transfer bumps generation and rev and holds every queued or held effect created under an older generation.
Transfer is a revisioned write; a stale expected revision changes nothing.
Transfer depends on prior state and must carry expected_revision.
Reusing an operation id with different content fails (409 operation_conflict).
The same operation id with the same payload digest is the same operation.
size counts UTF-8 bytes (5 for café), not characters.
size equals the UTF-8 byte length of text.
An empty text has size 0.
Both positions approve.
No change needed is a first-class outcome.
Mixed approvals combine to APPROVE (the mapping §10 leaves to the review schemas).
Any REJECT goes to the operator, even in round 1.
Any INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE goes to the operator.
REJECT escalates before any disagreement rule applies.
A FLAG with an approval is a disagreement; round 1 gets the single corrective re-review (Odin's provisional reading pending issue X-7).
A disagreement that survives the re-review goes to the operator.
Two FLAGs agree that the artifact needs the operator (pinned Saga contract ADM-7): escalated in any round. Odin's provisional reading pending issue X-7.
Two FLAGs escalate in round 2 as in round 1. Odin's provisional reading pending issue X-7.
An unavailable position never waives required review; one approval alone is not approved.
Any REJECT escalates unconditionally, so the rejection reaches the operator; the unavailable position still never waives review.
Neither position has answered.
A process that died between action and receipt leaves the effect unknown on restart.
Nothing was in flight.
Saga's lookup reports completed with the original receipt.
Pending: wait.
Failed is recorded as failed.
A guidance operation Saga reports superseded is never re-sent.
superseded is a lookup answer for guidance only (§9: "superseded (guidance only)"); for a run submission it is invalid input.
Confirmed absence within the retention window allows a retry with the same operation id.
An aged-out record is not confirmed absence: stays unknown and goes to the operator.
A plain notification is never auto-resent.
A request is resent with the same request id and digest.
An approval request is resent with the same request id and digest.
An attention prompt is never auto-resent; it counts against the caps.
While the host is offline a queued command stays queued and is not retried.
An in-flight command to an offline host becomes unknown (§9: "or unknown if one was in flight") and is not retried.
An unknown command stays unknown while the host is offline.
On return the host's report confirms the command.
On return the host reports it never received the command: retry with the same operation id.
A lookup value outside B-13's set is refused.
Telegram has no lookup; supplying one is invalid input.
Only :notify, :request and :approval have an irreducibly-unknown policy.
A session-host command is reconciled only with the host's state.
A returned host reports completed or absent.
Only unknown (or, for a session host, queued and in_flight) effects are reconciled.
A shadow-mode prompt is logged and never dispatched.
An effect created under a superseded owner generation is cancelled.
A revoked delegation cancels its pending effects.
An effect for a cancelled assignment is cancelled.
An effect for a completed assignment is cancelled.
An expired approval cannot authorize dispatch.
Checks run in order owner_generation, delegation_revoked, assignment_state, approval_expired.
Current authority: the effect stays queued.
A held effect leaves held only through revalidation, here to queued.
A held effect whose generation was superseded is cancelled.
An effect held by take-control at the current generation stays held while the take-control is in force; it is not released by revalidation.
Once the take-control that held it is returned, revalidation releases the effect to queued when every authority check passes.
An effect created under no owner generation and no assignment skips those checks.
Only queued and held effects are revalidated.
Dispatch is disabled until recovery step 8.
The recovery check comes first.
A queued effect outside recovery is dispatched and becomes in_flight.
The dispatcher revalidates before dispatch: a queued effect created under a superseded owner generation is cancelled, never sent.
The dispatcher revalidates before dispatch: a queued effect whose delegation was revoked is cancelled, never sent.
Only a queued effect is dispatched; a held one must be revalidated first.
The heimdall mapping validates against its schema.
Every commitment field is covered by at least one row.
A mapping without rows for two fields reports them, sorted.
